newsitem.title: JAPAN: NTT agrees 12 pct cut in access charges to 3 firms.
newsitem.headline: NTT agrees 12 pct cut in access charges to 3 firms.

text.p: Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp and three long-distance operators said on Wednesday they had agreed to a 12 percent cut in interconnection charges that the three firms pay to NTT for using its local loops.

After prolonged negotiations with DDI Corp , Japan Telecom Co and Teleway Japan Co, NTT has agreed to reduce the rate per three minutes to 9.20 yen for the year to March 31, 1997, down from the 1995/96 rate of 10.46 yen.
NTT, which monopolises local call networks, will apply the rate retroactively to April 1996.
The three long-distance operators at present pay about half of their revenues to NTT as interconnection charges.
NTT cut the rate by 16.7 percent in 1995/96.
DDI has already announced an upward revision of its estimated 1996/97 business results, citing the effects of access charge cuts.
Following the agreement with long-distance operators, NTT is to begin talks with cellular phone operators, cable television companies and international call operators on new access charges.
